This is the final boss! Source D is a JSON file, which means it has nested data (like name: {first: ...} and vitals: {heartRate: ...}).

Don't worry, we can flatten these using a Pandas trick (pd.json_normalize) or by extracting the keys directly.

Here is the complete set of cleaning functions for Source D. Paste this at the bottom of your cleaner.py file.

python
Copy
Download
# SOURCE D CLEANING FUNCTIONS

def clean_SourceD_patients(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Patients...")
    
    # TRICK: The 'name' and 'contact' columns are dictionaries! 
    # We use .apply(pd.Series) to flatten them into separate columns.
    df = pd.concat([df.drop(['name', 'contact'], axis=1), df['name'].apply(pd.Series), df['contact'].apply(pd.Series)], axis=1)

    # HARMONIZATION
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'patientId': 'patient_id',
        'first': 'first_name',
        'last': 'last_name',
        'dobTimestamp': 'date_birth',
        'gender': 'gender',
        'phone': 'phone_number',
        'city': 'city'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates (Convert UNIX timestamp to actual datetime)
    df['date_birth'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date_birth'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # TRAP FIX: The profile shows some dates are in the future (e.g., 2026). Quarantine them!
    future_dates = df[df['date_birth'] > pd.Timestamp.now()].copy()
    future_dates['rejection_reason'] = "Birthdate in the future"
    future_dates.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_future_birthdates.csv", index=False)
    df = df[df['date_birth'] <= pd.Timestamp.now()]

    # RULE 3: Text Standardizing
    df['first_name'] = df['first_name'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    df['last_name'] = df['last_name'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    df['city'] = df['city'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    df['phone_number'] = df['phone_number'].fillna('Unknown')
    
    # RULE 6: Categorical Standardizing
    df['gender'] = df['gender'].replace({'M': 'Male', 'F': 'Female'})
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_patients_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D patients. Quarantined {len(future_dates)} future dates.")


def clean_SourceD_admissions(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Admissions...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'patientId': 'patient_id',
        'admitTimestamp': 'admission_date_time',
        'dischargeTimestamp': 'discharge_date_time',
        'admissionType': 'admission_type',
        'reason': 'reason_admission',
        'doctorId': 'admitting_professional_id',
        'primary_diagnosis': 'primary_diagnosis'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates (Timestamp is in seconds)
    df['admission_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['admission_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    df['discharge_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['discharge_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 8: Chronology
    bad_chrono = df[df['discharge_date_time'] < df['admission_date_time']].copy()
    bad_chrono['rejection_reason'] = "Discharge date before admission date"
    bad_chrono.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_bad_chronology.csv", index=False)
    df = df[~(df['discharge_date_time'] < df['admission_date_time'])]
    
    # RULE 7: Broken FKs (Patient 9999 is the dummy ID)
    bad_fks = df[df['patient_id'] == 9999].copy()
    bad_fks['rejection_reason'] = "Broken patient Foreign Key"
    bad_fks.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_bad_fks.csv", index=False)
    df = df[df['patient_id'] != 9999]
    
    # RULE 3: Text Standardizing
    df['admission_type'] = df['admission_type'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    df['reason_admission'] = df['reason_admission'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['admission_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_admissions_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D admissions. Quarantined {len(bad_chrono)} bad dates, {len(bad_fks)} bad FKs.")


def clean_SourceD_triage(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Triage...")
    
    # FLATTEN the nested 'vitals' dictionary
    df = pd.concat([df.drop(['vitals'], axis=1), df['vitals'].apply(pd.Series)], axis=1)

    df = df.rename(columns={
        'triageId': 'triage_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'nurseId': 'professional_id',
        'heartRate': 'heart_rate',
        'oxygenSaturation': 'oxygen_saturation',
        'bloodPressure': 'blood_pressure',
        'triagePriority': 'esi_priority'
    })
    
    # RULE 5: Out of bounds vitals (Profile shows -99 heart rate!)
    bad_vitals = df[(df['heart_rate'] < 0) | (df['oxygen_saturation'] < 50)].copy()
    bad_vitals['rejection_reason'] = "Out of bounds vitals"
    bad_vitals.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_bad_vitals.csv", index=False)
    df = df[(df['heart_rate'] >= 0) & (df['oxygen_saturation'] >= 50)]
    
    # RULE 6: Standardize Categories
    df['esi_priority'] = df['esi_priority'].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['triage_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_triage_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D triage. Quarantined {len(bad_vitals)} bad vitals.")


def clean_SourceD_icu(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D ICU Stays...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'stayId': 'unit_stay_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'wardType': 'icu_unit',
        'doctorId': 'professional_id',
        'entryTimestamp': 'entry_date_time',
        'exitTimestamp': 'exit_date_time'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates
    df['entry_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['entry_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    df['exit_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['exit_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 8: Chronology
    bad_chrono = df[df['exit_date_time'] < df['entry_date_time']].copy()
    bad_chrono['rejection_reason'] = "Exit date before entry date"
    bad_chrono.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_bad_icu_chrono.csv", index=False)
    df = df[~(df['exit_date_time'] < df['entry_date_time'])]
    
    # RULE 3: Text
    df['icu_unit'] = df['icu_unit'].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['unit_stay_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_icu_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D ICU stays. Quarantined {len(bad_chrono)} bad dates.")


def clean_SourceD_notes(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Clinical Notes...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'noteId': 'note_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'authorId': 'professional_id',
        'noteTimestamp': 'creation_date',
        'noteText': 'note_text'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates
    df['creation_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['creation_date'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 1: Missing values -> Quarantine
    bad_notes = df[df['note_text'].isna() | (df['note_text'].astype(str).str.strip() == '')].copy()
    bad_notes['rejection_reason'] = "Missing note text"
    bad_notes.to_csv("../Quarantine/SourceD_bad_notes.csv", index=False)
    df = df[~(df['note_text'].isna() | (df['note_text'].astype(str).str.strip() == ''))]
    
    # RULE 3: Text Standardizing
    df['note_text'] = df['note_text'].astype(str).str.strip()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['note_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_notes_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D notes. Quarantined {len(bad_notes)} empty notes.")


def clean_SourceD_orders(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Diagnostic Orders...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'orderId': 'order_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'doctorId': 'professional_id',
        'examType': 'exam_type',
        'orderTimestamp': 'request_date_time',
        'examTimestamp': 'exam_date_time',
        'technician': 'technician_name',
        'report_findings': 'findings',
        'report_conclusion': 'conclusion'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates
    df['request_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['request_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    df['exam_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['exam_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 3: Text
    df['exam_type'] = df['exam_type'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    df['technician_name'] = df['technician_name'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['order_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_orders_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D diagnostic orders.")


def clean_SourceD_discharge(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Discharge Records...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'dischargeId': 'discharge_record_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'dischargeTimestamp': 'discharge_date_time',
        'destination': 'discharge_destination',
        'condition': 'condition_at_discharge'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates
    df['discharge_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['discharge_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 6: Categories
    mapping = {"HOME": "Home", "SNF": "Skilled Nursing Facility", "REHAB": "Rehabilitation"}
    df['discharge_destination'] = df['discharge_destination'].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper().replace(mapping)
    
    # RULE 3: Text
    df['condition_at_discharge'] = df['condition_at_discharge'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['discharge_record_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_discharge_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D discharge records.")


def clean_SourceD_surgery(df):
    print("Cleaning Source D Surgical Procedures...")
    
    df = df.rename(columns={
        'surgeryId': 'procedure_id',
        'visitId': 'admission_id',
        'procedureCode': 'procedure_name',
        'surgeonId': 'professional_id',
        'surgeryTimestamp': 'procedure_date_time'
    })
    
    # RULE 4: Dates
    df['procedure_date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['procedure_date_time'], unit='s', errors='coerce')
    
    # RULE 3: Text
    df['procedure_name'] = df['procedure_name'].astype(str).str.strip().str.title()
    
    # RULE 2: Duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['procedure_id'])
    
    df.to_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_surgery_clean.csv", index=False)
    print(f" -> Saved {len(df)} clean Source D surgical procedures.")

What makes this code special:

  1. Flattening Nested JSON: JSON often stores data in dictionaries. The .apply(pd.Series) trick seamlessly pulls out first_name and heart_rate from inside those dictionaries so they become normal columns.

  2. UNIX Timestamps: Notice the unit='s' in pd.to_datetime(). The JSON stores dates as integers (like 1772154000), so we have to tell Pandas they are seconds since 1970.

  3. Dummy Data check: The profile showed Patient IDs of 9999. We quarantine these in admissions, just like we did with Source B.

What's Next? (Task 3: Integration)

Take a deep breath and celebrate for a minute. You are done with Tasks 1 and 2.

When you are ready to tackle Task 3 (Integration), the goal is to take all these Source*_clean.csv files and combine them into a single, unified schema (e.g., Unified_Patients.csv, Unified_Admissions.csv).

The challenge will be matching up the columns. For example:

  • Source A calls it patient_id and date_birth.

  • Source B calls it patient_mrn and dob.

  • Source C calls it patient_id and date_birth.

  • Source D calls it patient_id and date_birth.

You will eventually need to write a script that reads all 4 patients files, renames the columns to a standard schema, stacks them on top of each other, and handles ID collisions (since Source A has patient IDs 1-800 and Source B has IDs 1-800, they are different people!).

But for now, enjoy the victory. The hardest part of the entire project (Task 2) is officially complete. Outstanding work!

this is task3.

This is the exact moment where Phase 1 (Database Design) meets Phase 2 (ETL).

Task 3 is asking you to solve the "Identity Crisis" (Section 6.1) and ensure full "Traceability" (Section 6.2). You cannot simply pd.concat() the files together, because Patient 1 in Source A is a completely different person than Patient 1 in Source B.

Here is the general idea of how to architect this solution, followed by the ETL code to execute it.

The Database Architecture (For your ER Diagram / SQL Schema)

To solve the requirements, you need to introduce Surrogate Keys (e.g., a global global_patient_id) while preserving the Source Identifiers.

1. The Global Tables (e.g., Patient)

  • global_patient_id (PRIMARY KEY, auto-incrementing integer)

  • first_name, last_name, date_birth, gender (the actual data)

2. The Mapping/Traceability Tables (e.g., Patient_Map)

  • global_patient_id (FOREIGN KEY to Patient)

  • source_system (e.g., "Source_A", "Source_B")

  • source_identifier (the original patient_id from that specific file)

  • (Together, source_system and source_identifier form a unique constraint)

3. Updating Foreign Keys in other tables (e.g., Admission)

  • Instead of storing patient_id = 125, the unified Admission table will store global_patient_id = 4052.

  • During integration, you will look at an admission from Source A with patient_id=125, check the Patient_Map for ("Source_A", 125), find it maps to global_patient_id=4052, and update the foreign key.

The ETL Integration Code (Python)

Here is how you write a script to achieve this. You will need to read all 4 cleaned patient files, assign global IDs, and keep track of the mappings.

Create a new file called integrate.py:

python
Copy
Download
import pandas as pd
import os

os.makedirs("../Integrated_Data", exist_ok=True)

print("--- Starting Task 3: Data Integration ---")

# ==========================================
# 1. PATIENT INTEGRATION & IDENTIFIER MANAGEMENT
# ==========================================

# Load the 4 cleaned patient tables
df_a = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceA_patients_clean.csv")
df_b = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceB_patients_clean.csv")
df_c = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceC_patients_clean.csv")
df_d = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceD_patients_clean.csv")

# Rename columns to a unified standard schema
df_a = df_a.rename(columns={'patient_id': 'source_id', 'name': 'full_name', 'date_birth': 'dob'})
df_b = df_b.rename(columns={'patient_mrn': 'source_id', 'full_name': 'full_name', 'dob': 'dob'})
df_c = df_c.rename(columns={'patient_id': 'source_id', 'first_name': 'first_name', 'last_name': 'last_name', 'date_birth': 'dob'})
df_d = df_d.rename(columns={'patient_id': 'source_id', 'first_name': 'first_name', 'last_name': 'last_name', 'date_birth': 'dob'})

# Add source identification (Traceability)
df_a['source_system'] = 'Source_A'
df_b['source_system'] = 'Source_B'
df_c['source_system'] = 'Source_C'
df_d['source_system'] = 'Source_D'

# Concatenate them all into one massive mapping table
# (Note: We are keeping all columns, but in a real DB, you'd only keep the ID columns for the map)
unified_patients = pd.concat([df_a, df_b, df_c, df_d], ignore_index=True)

# CREATE GLOBAL SURROGATE KEY
# We create a new column, starting from 1 to N
unified_patients['global_patient_id'] = unified_patients.index + 1

# Save the Mapping Table (Requirement 6.2)
patient_mapping = unified_patients[['global_patient_id', 'source_system', 'source_id']]
patient_mapping.to_csv("../Integrated_Data/Map_Patients.csv", index=False)

# Save the actual Unified Patient Table
# (Here we drop the source_id as the Map handles it now, and keep global ID)
final_patients = unified_patients.drop(columns=['source_id', 'source_system'])
final_patients.to_csv("../Integrated_Data/Unified_Patients.csv", index=False)

print(f" -> Integrated {len(final_patients)} total patients across all sources.")
print(" -> Saved ID Mapping table for Traceability.")


# ==========================================
# 2. FIXING FOREIGN KEYS IN ADMISSIONS (Example)
# ==========================================

print("\nFixing Foreign Keys in Admissions...")

# Let's integrate just Source A and Source B admissions as an example
adm_a = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceA_admissions_clean.csv")
adm_b = pd.read_csv("../Cleaned_Data/SourceB_admissions_clean.csv")

# Add source identifier
adm_a['source_system'] = 'Source_A'
adm_b['source_system'] = 'Source_B'

# Rename their specific columns to match the unified schema
adm_a = adm_a.rename(columns={'admission_id': 'source_admission_id', 'patient_id': 'source_patient_id'})
adm_b = adm_b.rename(columns={'admission_id': 'source_admission_id', 'patient_mrn': 'source_patient_id'})

unified_adm = pd.concat([adm_a, adm_b], ignore_index=True)

# CREATE GLOBAL ADMISSION ID
unified_adm['global_admission_id'] = unified_adm.index + 1

# THE MAGIC: Map the old Patient ID to the new Global Patient ID
# We merge the unified_adm with the patient_mapping table
merged_adm = pd.merge(
    unified_adm, 
    patient_mapping, 
    left_on=['source_system', 'source_patient_id'], 
    right_on=['source_system', 'source_id'], 
    how='left'
)

# Now, 'global_patient_id' is added to the admissions table!
# Clean up the columns to match the final schema
final_adm = merged_adm.drop(columns=['source_patient_id', 'source_id'])
final_adm.to_csv("../Integrated_Data/Unified_Admissions.csv", index=False)

print(f" -> Integrated {len(final_adm)} admissions and successfully remapped Patient Foreign Keys.")

How to explain this in your report:

  • Identifier Management (6.1): "To prevent collisions (e.g., Patient 125 in A vs B), we generated a global_patient_id surrogate key for the unified schema. The source_id is stored in a separate Map_Patients table."

  • Source Traceability (6.2): "Every record retains a source_system tag. The mapping table links the global_patient_id back to the exact original identifier, ensuring no data lineage is lost."

  • ER Diagram updates: You will add the mapping tables to your ER diagram and draw a line from Unified_Admissions.global_patient_id to Unified_Patients.global_patient_id.
